name: Fredrik Anfinsen
current_role: Co-founder & Senior Principal Architect, Cognite (Norway)
profile: Norwegian software engineer and co-founder of Cognite, the Oslo-founded (2016) industrial DataOps/AI company behind Cognite Data Fusion, backed by Aker and used by BP, Aramco and Aker BP. Previously founded and ran 3D file-sharing startup ShareMy3D. Still at Cognite in a senior technical (architect) role rather than an executive one.
interesting_fact: Cognite's platform contextualises raw industrial sensor/OT data for heavy-asset sectors (oil & gas, power, renewables); customers include BP, Aker BP, Saudi Aramco and Statnett.
deep_cut_fact: Before Cognite he co-founded ShareMy3D in Oslo (with Kaye Hope), a browser-based service pitched as making sharing 3D models (up to 5 GB) as easy as sharing a YouTube video.
notes: Low public profile; technical co-founder (not CEO). Founder attribution for Cognite is often given to John Markus Lervik et al.; Anfinsen listed as co-founder by Cognite job pages/MarketScreener. Best route: Cognite media relations.

name: Karim Pichara Baksai
current_role: Co-founder & CTO, NotCo; associate professor of computer science, Pontificia Universidad Católica de Chile
profile: Chilean computer scientist who co-founded NotCo (2015, Santiago) with Matías Muchnick and Pablo Zamora and built 'Giuseppe', the AI that reverse-engineers animal products from plant ingredients. NotCo became a ~$1.5B+ unicorn, struck a JV with Kraft Heinz, and is pushing its AI platform to B2B clients (incl. fragrance/flavour formulation).
interesting_fact: Before food, he applied machine learning to astronomy: TechCrunch described him as an astrophysicist using data science to explore the inner workings of stars, and he did a 2011-12 Harvard postdoc in ML for astronomy.
deep_cut_fact: He co-authored 'Meta-Classification for Variable Stars' (Astrophysical Journal, 2016) with Harvard's Pavlos Protopapas, and still publishes on automatic variable-star classification (e.g. streaming classifiers, MNRAS 2020).

public_contacts.value: Rachel Kay Public Relations - notco@rkpr.net (US media contact on NotCo releases, 2022-23)

notes: Academic as well as founder; likely receptive to AI/data angles. PR agency contact is from 2023 releases and may be outdated.

name: David Arana
current_role: Co-founder & CEO, Konfío (Mexico City)
profile: Mexican fintech founder who left a VP role structuring Latin American credit derivatives at Deutsche Bank (NY) in March 2013 to co-found Konfío with Francisco Padilla. Konfío provides data-driven loans, corporate cards and SaaS tools to Mexican SMEs and reached a $1B+ valuation in 2021; it has pursued a banking licence.
interesting_fact: MIT mathematics graduate; Konfío's early model was to lend to small firms that micro-finance (group lending) and banks both ignored, using alternative data for underwriting.
deep_cut_fact: In a 2016 LAVCA interview he said he and Padilla first 'started building something basic' to lend to tiny companies just to see 'if we would get the money back' - Konfío began as a viability test, not a grand plan.
notes: Konfío press releases route media via named staff and the agency 'another'; no general press inbox found. Speaker at AS/COA and IFC podcasts.

name: Peter Quinn
current_role: Listed as a co-founder of Public.com (Public Holdings); current role unconfirmed
profile: Named in several broker reviews as one of Public.com's founders (with Jannick Malling, Matt Kennedy and Sean Hendelman); Public is a US commission-free investing app now run by co-CEOs Leif Abraham and Malling. No reliable biography or current role found.
interesting_fact: Public.com, which he is credited with co-founding, launched in 2019 as a 'social investing' app and in 2025 launched an AI-powered brokerage.
notes: Common name; could not confirm identity or current involvement from primary sources. Treat with caution; route via Public press.

name: Derek Slager
current_role: Co-founder & co-CEO (also CTO), Amperity (Seattle)
profile: Seattle engineer who co-founded customer data platform Amperity (2016) with Kabir Shahani after both were on the founding team of Appature (acquired by IMS Health). He built Amperity's patented ML-based identity resolution; the company hit a $1B valuation in 2020. Now co-CEO leading its AI-first transformation.
interesting_fact: Amperity uses machine learning rather than hand-written rules to resolve customer identity, stitching together billions of records across a brand's systems; the patented identity resolution was built under Slager.
deep_cut_fact: Before Amperity and Appature he was a software developer at Seattle-era companies Activate, Loudeye (an early digital-music/streaming firm) and Blue Dot, then ran engineering at IMS Health after Appature's acquisition.
notes: Frequent podcast guest (NVIDIA AI Podcast 2025, Databricks Data+AI Summit speaker). Amperity site titles vary (CTO vs co-CEO).

name: Chris Eigeland
current_role: Co-founder & CEO, Go1 (Brisbane)
profile: Australian co-founder of Go1, the Brisbane-born (2015, Y Combinator S15) corporate learning-content aggregator, started by four school friends. Former CRO and co-CEO, he became sole CEO in August 2024. Go1 was valued at $2B+ in 2022.
interesting_fact: Go1 went through Y Combinator's Summer 2015 batch and became one of Australia's first edtech unicorns, aggregating training content into whatever LMS a company already uses.
deep_cut_fact: A Griffith law graduate and trained international lawyer, he was Australia's Youth Representative to the United Nations in 2016 and gave a TEDx talk in 2015.

name: Ben Kinney
current_role: Co-founder, PLACE Inc.; founder, Ben Kinney Companies (BKCO)
profile: Washington-state real estate agent turned proptech entrepreneur. Founded BKCO (Brivity, ActiveRain, Kwkly, Blueroof360) and in 2019 co-founded PLACE with Chris Suarez, a platform/services company for top real-estate teams that raised $100M led by Goldman Sachs at a $1B valuation in 2021.
interesting_fact: He was the top-ranked agent in Washington state by transaction volume from 2012 to 2021 and appeared on the WSJ/REAL Trends top-1,000 agents lists 2011-2022.
deep_cut_fact: While studying at Western Washington University he worked as a cable-TV installer, then sold cable, phone and internet door-to-door before starting in real estate in 2004.
notes: Active speaker and author (Inman, RISMedia). PLACE reportedly eyeing an IPO.

name: Wu Yun
current_role: Founder & CEO, XforcePlus (Shanghai Yunli Information Technology / 票易通)
profile: Chinese enterprise-software founder (吴云, 'Will Woo') who set up XforcePlus in 2015 to digitise VAT invoices and supply-chain/finance/tax collaboration for large enterprises. Backed by Temasek (2019 Series C ~$100M) and a 2021 round at ~$1B valuation. Company filings show him holding the large majority of the operating entity.
interesting_fact: Described as a China supply-chain/finance/tax IT expert who led construction of what was billed as China's largest cloud-deployed financial shared-services platform before founding XforcePlus.
deep_cut_fact: Named to Fortune China's 2020 '40 Under 40' business list and is a member of Tsinghua SEM's entrepreneur-scholar DBA programme.
notes: Chinese-language outreach advisable; no press email found.

name: Mauricio Chamati
current_role: Founder & CEO, Jumpad (AI governance startup); co-founder and board member of 2TM (Mercado Bitcoin holding)
profile: Brazilian technologist who co-founded Mercado Bitcoin (2013, with brother Gustavo) and its holding company 2TM, which became Brazil's first crypto unicorn (~$2.1B, 2021 SoftBank-led round). He served as Mercado Bitcoin's CTO, moved to the 2TM board in 2019, and in Oct 2025 launched Jumpad, which helps companies manage corporate AI use.
interesting_fact: Mercado Bitcoin started in 2013 when bitcoin was barely known in Brazil and grew into Latin America's largest crypto exchange.
deep_cut_fact: His new startup Jumpad launched with offices in São Paulo and Belo Horizonte, 10 beta clients and a pre-seed round (Oct 2025).
notes: Also linked to Gear Ventures (fintech VC). Speaker at South Summit. Avoid founder-credit dispute raised by an ex-executive.

name: John Lafleur
current_role: Co-founder & COO, Airbyte (San Francisco)
profile: French serial entrepreneur who co-founded Airbyte (2020, YC) with CEO Michel Tricot; the open-source data-integration/ELT platform reached a ~$1.5B valuation in 2021. Earlier ventures: As-App, StreamNation (acquired by SmugMug), CodinGame (COO/CEO) and Anaxi.
interesting_fact: Airbyte started in YC as Daxtarity, a marketing-data tool, and pivoted during COVID after customer interviews revealed teams were hand-building data pipelines.
deep_cut_fact: His entrepreneurial career began in 2008 with As-App, a ski-resort app later acquired by Lumiplan.

public_contacts.value: Joe Eckert, Eckert Communications - jeckert@eckertcomms.com (Airbyte media contact)

notes: Writes about developer marketing/open source; dev.to profile is his own blog, labelled substack type for lack of a better field.

name: Felipe Capella
current_role: Co-founder & CEO, Loadsmart (New York)
profile: Brazilian-born former corporate/M&A lawyer who co-founded freight-tech company Loadsmart with Ricardo Salgado in 2014. Loadsmart offers AI-driven brokerage, TMS (ShipperGuide), dock scheduling (Opendock) and in 2026 an AI-agent platform; it reached unicorn status in 2022. CEO since 2022 after serving as CPO, COO and co-CEO.
interesting_fact: Loadsmart claims the first fully automated truckload shipment (2016), booked and priced with no human involvement.
deep_cut_fact: He is an amateur photographer who plays guitar, piano and the Brazilian cavaquinho, has visited 47 countries, and holds a US 'Extraordinary Ability in Business' visa.

public_contacts.value: felipe@loadsmart.com (listed as media contact on Loadsmart's 2026 AI-agents release)

notes: Frequent podcast guest (Logistics of Logistics, FreightWaves). His own address appears as media contact on a 2026 release; verify before use.

name: Xue Suwen
current_role: Chairman & President, Nxin Group (农信互联 / 农信数智), Beijing
profile: Chinese agri-tech executive (薛素文), formerly executive VP of feed and agri giant Dabeinong, who leads Nxin, the Dabeinong-affiliated platform founded 2015 whose 'Pig Internet' (猪联网) digitises hog farming - farm management, trading and financing. Nxin is valued around $1B.
interesting_fact: Nxin's Pig Internet sized the hog industry chain at nearly RMB 3 trillion and has connected tens of millions of pigs on its platform.
deep_cut_fact: At 2017's T-EDGE he quipped that if Nxin is an internet company, it must be one 'full of the smell of soil - or even pig manure' (充满泥土味/猪粪味道的互联网企业).
notes: Chinese-language outreach advisable. Hurun lists him as founder; he is chairman/president (Nxin was incubated by Dabeinong).

name: Young-il Lee
current_role: Founder & CEO, HAEGIN (Seoul)
profile: Korean mobile-games veteran and co-founder of Com2uS who founded HAEGIN in Sept 2017. Its social game Play Together (2021) became a global hit with 200M+ downloads; HAEGIN raised a $110M Series B in 2022 from Kakao Games, Netmarble, SK Square and others.
interesting_fact: 'Haegin' means 'living long and happily' in old Korean; over 90% of the company's traffic and revenue comes from outside Korea.
deep_cut_fact: Lee co-founded Com2uS, one of Korea's pioneering mobile game makers, and later served as its EVP for Far East business before starting HAEGIN.
notes: $8B figure in source list looks inflated; public reports suggest ~$1B+ unicorn status.

name: Michael Gilbert
current_role: Founder, Semios (Vancouver); CEO until Amie Thesingh's appointment in late 2025 - current title unconfirmed
profile: Canadian chemist (PhD, UBC) who founded Semios in 2010 to bring pheromone-based mating disruption and wireless orchard sensors to growers, reducing pesticide use. Semios grew into an ag-data platform covering 100M+ acres.
interesting_fact: Semios pairs aerosol pheromone dispensers with a wireless sensor network, confusing pests like codling moth so they can't mate instead of killing them with sprays.
deep_cut_fact: He told the Georgia Straight that pheromones, though well understood, were used on 'less than one per cent of the farms that could be using them' - and that 'farmers are always environmentalists'.
notes: Common name; confirmed via Semios coverage. The Semios Group named Amie Thesingh CEO (Sept/Oct 2025).

name: Jack Lu
current_role: Co-founder & CEO, Magic Eden
profile: Chinese-Australian former Google product manager and BCG consultant (also briefly at FTX) who co-founded Solana NFT marketplace Magic Eden in 2021; it became a $1.6B unicorn in nine months. In Feb/Mar 2026 he refocused the company on Solana and its crypto casino/sportsbook Dicey, shutting Bitcoin/EVM marketplaces.
interesting_fact: Magic Eden hit unicorn status (Series B, $130M at $1.6B) in June 2022, roughly nine months after launch.
deep_cut_fact: His first job (2014) was as a software engineer at Hello Block, an early developer API for the Bitcoin blockchain.
notes: Deep-cut source is a secondary profile; verify before using. Company pivot to iGaming in 2026.

name: Matan Liberman
current_role: Co-founder & EVP Business Development; head of Israel operations and R&D, Semperis
profile: Israeli co-founder of Semperis (with CEO Mickey Bresman and CTO Guy Teverovsky), the Hoboken/Tel Aviv identity-security company specialising in Active Directory protection and recovery. Semperis became a unicorn with a $125M round in 2023 (Calcalist's most promising Israeli startup of 2023).
interesting_fact: He told Calcalist Semperis was 'a strange bird' - its founders did not come from the IDF's elite intelligence tech units that produce most Israeli cyber startups.
deep_cut_fact: He began as a software engineer in the IDF implementing mission-critical systems for the Office of the Israeli Prime Minister, later leading development of an organisational identity-management system.

public_contacts.value: billk@semperis.com (Bill Keeler, Sr. Director PR & Comms)

name: Arsen Tomsky
current_role: Founder & CEO, inDrive
profile: Yakutsk-born (1973) entrepreneur, now a Kazakh citizen, who built Yakutia's largest internet company (Sinet/Ykt.ru) and in 2013 launched inDriver, whose riders propose fares that drivers accept or counter. inDrive (renamed 2022) has expanded across Latin America, Africa, South Asia and beyond, became a top-2 downloaded ride-hailing app, and in 2026 he is launching free universities (inVision U).
interesting_fact: inDrive was born from a Yakutsk social-media group of drivers created to fight taxi-fare price-gouging during brutal winter cold; its fare-negotiation model now challenges Uber in emerging markets.
deep_cut_fact: His first business (1994) was software: a system for analysing banks' financial condition, then an automated accounting program commissioned by Yakutia's Ministry of Finance, before graduating in mathematics in 1995.
notes: Writes op-eds (Entrepreneur, 2026, on robotaxis in emerging markets). inDrive uses regional PR (e.g. Square Inches PR in India); no global press inbox found.

name: Kavitha Subramanian
current_role: Co-founder, Upstox (growth, strategy, finance and customer experience)
profile: Indian fintech co-founder who, with Ravi Kumar and Shrini Viswanath, built Upstox (RKSV), a Mumbai discount broker backed by Tiger Global and Ratan Tata that became a unicorn in 2021 with 10M+ users. IIT Bombay electrical engineer and Wharton MBA, formerly at McKinsey and private-equity firms Actis and LeapFrog.
interesting_fact: She is one of relatively few women co-founders of an Indian fintech unicorn; Upstox scaled past 10 million users during the 2020-21 retail investing boom.
deep_cut_fact: Before Upstox she was an associate director at impact investor LeapFrog Investments and an investment principal at emerging-markets PE firm Actis.
notes: Frequently quoted on women investors and financial literacy (Zee Business).

name: Zhang Tingchao
current_role: Legal representative of Hangzhou Valgen Medtech (德晋医疗); exact title unconfirmed
profile: Listed by Hurun as founder of Valgen Medtech, the Hangzhou structural-heart device maker (founded 2015) behind the DragonFly transcatheter mitral clip. Corporate records show 张庭超 (Zhang Tingchao) as legal representative; CEO is listed as Zhao Yiwei. Valgen raised a Series B from DCP, HongShan and Qiming.
interesting_fact: Valgen's DragonFly was approved by China's NMPA in Nov 2023 as the first homegrown transcatheter device to repair a leaky mitral valve, and later won a CE mark in Europe.
notes: Could not find a biography; founder status rests on Hurun and registry (legal rep). Keep outreach to the company.

name: John Carolan
current_role: Co-founder & Chief of Quality Assurance, ThreatLocker (Orlando)
profile: Co-founded zero-trust endpoint security company ThreatLocker in 2017 with Danny and Sami Jenkins; the company launched with application allowlisting ('default deny') and now protects 50,000+ businesses, reaching a $1B+ valuation. He leads quality assurance.
interesting_fact: ThreatLocker's default-deny model blocks every application action unless explicitly allowed - the opposite of traditional antivirus.
notes: Very low public profile; no standalone bio published. Best route: ThreatLocker press.
